subject: CardioHealth Sprint 0: kickoff, schema handoff, and implementation sprint plan
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardiohealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cardiohealth.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: CardioHealth Sprint 0 kickoff & schema handoff

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about live streaming + tool calling for our clinician-assist workflow. We want to move quickly into Sprint 0 to validate latencies, structured output formats (JSON), and a small alpha using function calls for EHR lookups.

Top priorities for us:
- Confirm streaming latency and prefix caching behavior for 1–2s response targets
- Agree on a JSON output schema for diagnosis summaries (minimal required fields)
- Verify secure tool calling to our internal EHR proxy (OAuth + scoped keys)

Can you share a Sprint 0 plan (milestones, owners, expected testers) and any starter JSON schema you recommend? Procurement is looped for timing on PO/DocuSign.

Attachments from our side: sample-patient-extract.csv (PII-scrubbed).

Best,
Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product Engineering, CardioHealth
alex.chen@cardiohealth.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardiohealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioHealth Sprint 0 kickoff & schema handoff

Alex — appreciate the clear priorities. Looping Jonas (sales) and Grace (solutions) so we can coordinate delivery and technical scope. Proposed Sprint 0 plan below (estimate 2 weeks):

Sprint 0: implementation sprint (2 weeks)
- Day 0: Kickoff call (Priya, Alex, Grace, engineer leads) — align on success criteria
- Day 1–3: Schema finalization & JSON contract (Grace lead) — produce schema-guidelines-v1.json
- Day 4–9: Streaming POC + prefix cache tuning (Redwood runtime team)
- Day 10–12: Tool-calling handshake + secure key exchange test (EHR proxy)
- Day 13–14: Acceptance testing with 5 clinician scenarios, latency + quality baseline

Owners and asks:
- CardioHealth: provide 3 representative clinician prompts and sample (PII-scrubbed) payloads
- Redwood: deliver initial JSON schema and a streaming POC environment (dev.redwood.cardio)
- Procurement: confirm PO/DocuSign timeline (we can run POC on trial credits if needed)

Attachments: sprint0-milestones.csv (milestones + owners), schema-guidelines-v1.json (starter).

Proposed kickoff: Wednesday 14 Apr 2027, 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
pri ya.natarajan@redwood.ai
---
Attachment: sprint0-milestones.csv (CSV stub: columns: milestone, owner, start_date, end_date)
Attachment: schema-guidelines-v1.json (JSON stub: top-level properties: patient_id, encounter_id, summary_text, confidence_score)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: CardioHealth Sprint 0 kickoff & schema handoff

Quick note from sales: CardioHealth indicated they want a short runway before legal signs — procurement looped in. If we can offer a 30-day POC credit (covered by the deal team) it will unblock the kickoff and allow Grace to run the EHR proxy tests without procurement gating. Priya — happy to approve the credit once we get a verbal ok from Alex.

Also tagging Grace: can you confirm required infra (VPC peering or token relay) so we know if Dedicated or Private is needed for the POC?

—Jonas

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardiohealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cardiohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioHealth Sprint 0 kickoff & schema handoff

Thanks Priya — plan looks good. Wednesday 14 Apr 10:00 AM PT works for the kickoff. Procurement: we can do a 30-day trial credit to expedite; procurement will still need a short MS (master services) and PO for records but we can sign DocuSign after initial acceptance.

Grace — for the EHR proxy test we prefer OAuth token relay; we'll share a test client and a scoped key. Please confirm if Redwood needs VPC peering or if token relay via HTTPS is sufficient for the Sprint 0 POC.

Also: can you send a draft JSON schema with required fields only (nothing proprietary)? We want to review tonight.
